l15-design-steps.title: A filter by demands, and the jump no sum can make
l15-design-steps.about: How a two-coefficient filter works, how to spend coefficients, and why the overshoot at a jump never goes away.

l15-overshoot-steps.title: Taming the overshoot

l15-window-steps.title: Windows: multiplying is convolving

l16-fft-steps.title: The FFT: fast, accurate, periodic, and blind to phase
l16-fft-steps.about: Hamming's idea for fewer multiplications, the FFT he refused, why it is also more accurate, what it assumes outside the record, and the phase the power spectrum drops.

l16-integrate-steps.title: Integration, a filter that must grow
l16-integrate-steps.about: Integration as a filter with unbounded gain at zero frequency, Hamming's new definition of stability, why the error grows like n squared on the moon, and why polynomial growth is acceptable.

l16-kaiser-steps.title: Kaiser's recipe: two tolerances in, a filter out
l16-kaiser-steps.about: How Kaiser turns a ripple tolerance and a ramp width into the number of weights and the window, how he found the formulas, why they work, and when they miss.

l16-spectrum-steps.title: Reading a spectrum: processing, noise, and linear tools
l16-spectrum-steps.about: What white noise in and a spectrum out tells you about a box, how standard processing makes a false peak, why sampled noise looks white, why oversampling helps, and what a flat spectrum does not prove.

l17-counts-steps.title: The physicist's counts

l17-echo-steps.title: A ratio and its echo
l17-echo-steps.about: What a feedback filter's ratio buys and costs, how sequence models run it two ways, and a feedback filter whose echo stops.

l17-feedback-steps.title: Feedback filters: the past only, both sides, and delay
l17-feedback-steps.about: Why a past-only smoother lags, how a two-sided one is solved, and why delay limits how hard a loop may correct.

l17-median-steps.title: The running median, and what linearity forces
l17-median-steps.about: A nonlinear filter that keeps jumps, what it costs on noise, and why every linear theory trades width in time for width in frequency.

p-complex.title: Primer · Complex numbers
p-complex.about: Complex numbers as arrows: what i does, multiplying, Euler's formula, real waves as shadows, sums and derivatives of arrows, each formula with its proof.

p-derivatives.title: Primer · Limits and derivatives
p-derivatives.about: Limits, the derivative as a slope, rules, peaks, partial derivatives, tangent lines, and differences of a table; each claim with a proof step.

p-feedback-1.title: Primer · Feedback: loops that settle, add up, or explode
p-feedback-1.about: Primer 0.16 (1 of 3): a difference equation makes each value from the last; a feedback loop turns one clap into 1, a, a^2, ...; a loss curve's moving average settles; with a steady input a loop settles, adds up or explodes; too strong a correction flips the error; why the gap to the resting value sh

p-feedback-2.title: Primer · Feedback: roots and swings
p-feedback-2.about: Primer 0.16 (2 of 3): a late correction swings (the shower); trying powers lambda^n gives the roots of a loop; every run is a mix of the powers; complex roots swing and shrink by |lambda| per step; a double root at 1 grows like n and n^2 (the moon landing).

p-feedback-3.title: Primer · Feedback: recursive filters and amplifiers
p-feedback-3.about: Primer 0.16 (3 of 3): a recursive filter feeds back its output and remembers forever; its gain H(f) is a ratio; it is stable when its roots lie inside the unit circle; negative feedback makes an amplifier's gain 1/beta (Black); positive feedback amplifies errors and squeals.

p-fourier.title: Primer · Fourier series
p-fourier.about: Primer 0.11: how waves add up to a shape, coefficients as projections, least squares, smoothness, and the discrete form with the FFT, each claim with a proof slide.

p-integrals-1.title: Primer · Integrals: accumulated area
p-integrals-1.about: What an integral is: area under a rate, rectangle sums, antiderivatives, averages, and the log rule, with a proof slide after each.

p-integrals-2.title: Primer · Integrals: techniques
p-integrals-2.about: How integrals are computed: substitution, integration by parts, an integral that defines a new function, why a polar patch is r dr dθ, and the bell-curve integral, with a proof slide for each.

p-least-squares.title: Primer · Least squares
p-least-squares.about: Least squares: the best line through points, why squares, the calculus of the fit, and the fit as a projection, each formula with its proof. Prepares Lecture 14.

p-logs-1.title: Primer · Exponentials
p-logs-1.about: Repeated multiplication, doubling time, e from compounding, decay and half-life, why an exponential beats a straight line, and a proof slide after each formula.

p-logs-2.title: Primer · Logarithms
p-logs-2.about: What a logarithm counts (doublings), why it turns products into sums, bases, log axes, decibels, and a proof slide after each formula.

p-matrices.title: Primer · Matrices and eigenvectors
p-matrices.about: Primer 0.09: a matrix as weighted sums, linearity, solving a small system, eigenvectors, and repeated steps, each claim with a proof slide.

p-sampling.title: Primer · Sampling and aliasing
p-sampling.about: Primer 0.07: sampling keeps readings, frequency as rotations per sample, how a fast wave can give the same dots as a slow one, samples per cycle, and rounding; each claim followed by its proof.

p-series.title: Primer · Series: geometric and Taylor
p-series.about: Ten slides: what an endless sum is worth, the geometric sum in one line, Taylor polynomials, where the ln(1+x) series fails, computing e^x and Bessel's I_0 term by term; after each, a proof slide (the halves reach 2, the geometric sum, the Taylor coefficients, the ln(1+x) error bound, the term recip

p-signals-1.title: Primer · Signals: what a filter does
p-signals-1.about: Primer 0.12 (1 of 4): a filter as sliding weights, the same filter as a matrix, the shift test, the echo of one tap, and why the shift test forces one row of weights.

p-signals-2.title: Primer · Signals: waves through a filter
p-signals-2.about: Primer 0.12 (2 of 4): a wave comes out of a filter with the same shape, scaled; the response H(f); a one-sided filter delays; complex waves as the filter's eigenvectors; a filter works wave by wave.

p-signals-3.title: Primer · Signals: convolution, filters in a row, short records
p-signals-3.about: Primer 0.12 (3 of 4): the output as a sum of echoes, two filters in a row as one filter (convolution), the product table, gains that multiply, and how a short record smears a tone; von Hann's window.

p-signals-4.title: Primer · Signals: spectra, phase and noise
p-signals-4.about: Primer 0.12 (4 of 4): the power spectrum ignores where a record starts, spectra of a sum do not add, white noise has a flat spectrum, and a derivative boosts noise by (2 pi f)^2.

p-vectors.title: Primer · Vectors
p-vectors.about: Primer 0.05: a vector as a list of numbers, its length, dot product and angle, the cube diagonal, projection, and distances (L1, L2, L-infinity); each claim followed by its proof.

p-waves.title: Primer · Waves: sine, cosine, frequency, phase
p-waves.about: Primer 0.03: what a sine wave is, what amplitude, frequency and phase do, radians, values to know, even and odd, adding waves, and the slope of a sine; each claim followed by its proof.
